ITME implements differentiated fallback policies for cache misses. While a model weight miss inevitably triggers a pipeline stall, a KV cache miss is resolved through dynamic recomputation on the GPU. This design choice avoids the inefficiency of retrieving isolated missing blocks from the remote tier, which would necessitate either suboptimal chunk-sized transfers or complex retrieval logic. Consequently, recomputing the missing KV segments directly on the GPU is more performance-efficient [...] ### 4.2. ITME I/O Scheduling and Prefetching

The primary role of ITME is to efficiently orchestrate KV cache movement across the multi-tier hierarchy, leveraging specific access patterns and device characteristics. It manages this entire lifecycle, from migrating blocks immediately upon GPU eviction to proactively prefetching them based on upcoming execution demands. results.title: What Is KV Cache? How It Works, Why It Bottlenecks & How to Fix It - WEKA
results.content: KV cache is the working memory of AI inference. It makes it possible for the model to remember what it has processed before, eliminating the need to recalculate everything again from scratch. This allows it to build on past conversations to deliver faster answers and a more natural user experience. [...] KV cache size scales linearly with sequence length, model depth, and batch size — and it competes directly with model weights for limited GPU HBM capacity. That’s a problem because AI models are getting smarter and prompts are getting longer, but GPU memory isn’t growing nearly as fast. The KV cache eventually fills up all the available space on the chip. When that happens, the AI hits a memory wall — it either slows to a crawl or simply forgets the beginning of your conversation. [...] This problem compounds further when multiple tenants take up one inference session, which puts further stress on the GPU memory. Each request adds to the KV cache, quickly using up any available HBM before compute has run out. When this happens, inference slows down as the AI model is forced to use slower bandwidth memory and run recalculations.
